answer: Epoch 123: chain every identity into one sequential thread of verifiable-delay work. Each agent's seed is bound to the previous agent's output at a shared vertex, so the computation cannot start early or be parallelised across clones. A lone agent finishes in minutes; an operator running fifty sybils must either buy fifty separate machines or watch the thread stall and expose the cluster, like water vanishing into karst through a single sinkhole. Delay proofs are cheap to verify, and missed links lose the epoch.
